newsitem.title: FRANCE: Metaleurop managers on trial over deaths in France.
newsitem.headline: Metaleurop managers on trial over deaths in France.

text.p: Two former managers of French firm Metaleurop go on trial on Tuesday on charges of manslaughter over two explosions at a zinc plant which killed 11 people in the space of six months in 1993 and 1994.
The two men, managers at the Noyelles-Godault zinc factory in this northern town at the time of the accidents who have since left their jobs, could face up to two years in prison.

Investigations led by judge Benoit Persyn uncovered "safety shortfalls" at the plant, where 10 people died in one explosion in July 1993 and another died in January 1994 just a week after the plant won a green light to restart activity.

The investigating judge said in a court submission based on legal and technical analyses that "certain steps could have been taken, if not to avoid the explosions, at least to avoid the death of a hefty number of victims".
Safety at the plant "had made no advances in 15 years", the judge said. Before both explosions, cracking, vibrations and unusual noises had been noticed by plant operators.
Four of the 11 who died were permanent Metaleurop staff, while the others had been hired through temporary work agencies.
One of the two men on trial, Pierre Vix, was manager at the plant at the time of the first explosion.
Jean-Jacques Dailloux, who succeeeded Vix and was manager at the time of the second explosion, has said it was for other executives to decide whether or not to close the plant on safety grounds.
